user.title: Set up power feedback and infrared commands
user.description: Select a frequently updated power sensor, the infrared emitter entity that transmits to your fan, and which Dyson Cool infrared code each fan command should send. The fan entity remains unavailable until several stable power reports have been received.

data_description.infrared_emitter_entity_id: An `infrared` platform emitter entity, such as an ESPHome infrared proxy.
data_description.power_toggle_code: The Dyson Cool code your fan's power button sends. Genuine Dyson remotes use separate ON/OFF codes rather than one toggle, so test which code this integration should use.
data_description.feedback_burst_action: Any Home Assistant action run against your power meter to request a faster report. Leave empty to skip this optimization.

data_description.infrared_emitter_entity_id: An `infrared` platform emitter entity, such as an ESPHome infrared proxy.
data_description.power_toggle_code: The Dyson Cool code your fan's power button sends. Genuine Dyson remotes use separate ON/OFF codes rather than one toggle, so test which code this integration should use.
data_description.feedback_burst_action: Any Home Assistant action run against your power meter to request a faster report. Leave empty to skip this optimization.

error.invalid_emitter: Select a valid infrared emitter entity.
error.invalid_code: Select a Dyson Cool infrared code for every required command.
error.invalid_action: The feedback-burst action is not a valid Home Assistant action sequence.
error.invalid_power_unit: Use a power unit such as W or kW, or no unit (assumed W).

abort.no_emitters: No infrared emitter entities found. Set up an infrared transmitter (for example, an ESPHome infrared proxy) first.

menu_option_descriptions.control: Change retry behavior and the interval between infrared transmissions.
menu_option_descriptions.power_table: Change off and stationary wattage and the shared oscillation increment.
menu_option_descriptions.ir_codes: Change the raw infrared timings used to encode every Dyson Cool command.

data_description.max_attempts: A complete initial command is one attempt. Additional attempts are only made after stable feedback does not match the target.
data_description.ir_send_interval: Time between consecutive infrared command transmissions.
data_description.stability_timeout_seconds: How long a reading may hold, uncontradicted, before it is accepted as stable even without 3 separate matching reports. Useful for report-on-change power sensors (e.g. some Zigbee plugs) that stay silent while the reading is unchanged.
data_description.calibration_mode: Endpoints shifts and scales the current curve from speeds 1 and 10. Full measures every stationary speed.

power_table.title: Power table
power_table.description: Enter the oscillation power increment followed by off and stationary power for speeds 1 through 10.

data.restore_default_power_table: Restore the built-in power table on submit

ir_codes.title: IR codes
ir_codes.description: Choose System to use infrared-protocols' own published-spec Dyson Cool timings unmodified, or Custom to set your own six raw timings on the next screen.

data_description.ir_timing_mode: System uses the library default timings. Custom lets you set your own.

ir_codes_custom.title: Custom IR timings
ir_codes_custom.description: Raw timings (in microseconds) used to build every transmitted infrared command. Defaults were measured against a physical Dyson AM07 remote.

data_description.ir_header_mark: Duration of the leading mark pulse.
data_description.ir_header_space: Duration of the space following the header mark.
data_description.ir_bit_mark: Duration of the mark pulse before every data bit.
data_description.ir_footer_mark: Duration of the trailing mark pulse.

error.invalid_power_table: Power values must increase with speed, and the oscillation increment must keep every value below 100 W.
